intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

selected_hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Walk & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Walk the clifftop trail connecting Marinha to Benagil and take a refreshing swim in the sheltered coves below.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local Algarve wineries such as Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor near Lagoa, sampling regional varieties including Negra Mole and Arinto. Guided tours typically include a cellar visit, explanation of the winemaking process, and a tasting flight of 4–6 wines paired with local cheeses and charcuterie.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of Portugal's most photographed natural wonders, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos and sea arches along the dramatic coastline, offering a unique perspective of the Algarve's geology and marine life.

experiences.name: Sagres & Cape St. Vincent Sunset Experience
experiences.description: Visit the southwestern-most tip of continental Europe at Cape St. Vincent, where dramatic cliffs plunge into the Atlantic. Explore the historic Sagres Fortress, stroll the windswept headland, and witness a breathtaking sunset over the ocean — a deeply cultural and natural highlight of any Algarve trip.
experiences.location: Sagres & Cape St. Vincent, Vila do Bispo

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour & Seafood Lunch
experiences.description: Take a guided boat tour through the Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park teeming with flamingos, herons, and other migratory birds. Stop at barrier island beaches like Ilha Deserta or Ilha do Farol, and enjoy a fresh seafood lunch featuring local clams, grilled fish, and regional white wine at a waterfront restaurant.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, clear customs, and arrange transfer to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay (approx. 1 hour drive from Faro Airport via EN125; use Rede Expressos bus or shared shuttle for budget ~€5–10 vs taxi ~€50).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Lagoa Boutique Stay, freshen up, then take a short 10-minute walk down to Praia da Marinha — one of the Algarve's most iconic beaches. Explore the golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear water. Swim or simply relax and soak in the surroundings after your journey.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the village of Lagoa or nearby Carvoeiro (5-minute drive / 20-minute walk) for a casual first dinner. Browse the small local restaurants along the beachfront strip.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or pastel de nata at the airport café before or after landing (€2–3).
meals.lunch: Pick up a sandwich or prego roll from a local padaria (bakery) near your accommodation on arrival (€3–5).
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro — a budget-friendly local tasca offering grilled fish of the day (peixe do dia) with salad and bread for €10–14. Pair with a glass of house Algarve wine (€1.50).

day_by_day.notes: September is ideal — summer crowds thin out, sea temperature is still warm (~23°C), and prices drop slightly. Book airport transfer in advance via Rede Expressos at redex.pt. Keep receipts for any transport for budget tracking.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning walk to Praia da Marinha before the day-trippers arrive (best light 8:00–10:00). Hike the dramatic clifftop trail toward Praia de Benagil (approx. 3 km one-way) — a free and stunning coastal path with sea arch views. Bring water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.afternoon: At Benagil, take a budget kayak or stand-up paddleboard rental (€15–20/hour) to paddle into the famous Benagil Sea Cave (Algar de Benagil) — one of the world's most beautiful sea caves. Alternatively, join a shared boat tour departing from Benagil beach (€10–15 per person for a 45-minute group trip). Swim inside the cave if conditions allow.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Carvoeiro village. Walk the boardwalk above Praia de Carvoeiro and watch the sunset from the clifftop viewpoint (Miradouro). Grab a beer or local Sagres beer at a beach bar (€2–3).

meals.breakfast: Café Calcinha in Carvoeiro — espresso (€0.80) and a tosta mista (toasted ham & cheese, €2.50) — a classic Portuguese budget breakfast.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the local mini-mercado: local bread, presunto (cured ham), queijo (cheese), olives, and fruit (€5–7 total). Eat at Benagil beach.
meals.dinner: A Tasca do Zé in Lagoa town — a beloved local workers' restaurant with daily specials (prato do dia) for €8–10 including soup, main, and a drink. Cash preferred.

day_by_day.notes: The Benagil cave can only be accessed by water — you cannot walk in. Book kayak/SUP rentals early in the day. The clifftop walk is free and one of the Algarve's best experiences. Wear sturdy sandals or trainers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve, 20 minutes inland from Lagoa (local bus from Lagoa town ~€2.50 each way). Explore the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves (castle entrance €2.80). Walk the old town walls and enjoy panoramic views over the orange groves and Arade River valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the Silves town center. Visit the Gothic Sé Catedral de Silves (free entry or small donation). Browse the weekly market if visiting on a Saturday, or explore the riverside promenade. Stop at a local adega (wine shop) — the Silves region is known for Algarve DOC wines. Many shops offer free tastings of local red and white wines.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa by bus. Relax at the accommodation. Optional: walk to a local supermarket (Pingo Doce or Lidl in Lagoa) to stock up on budget supplies — local wine bottles start at €3–5.

meals.breakfast: At accommodation or a local café in Lagoa — galão (milky coffee, €1.20) and croissant (€1.50).
meals.lunch: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — famous for cataplana (traditional seafood stew) but also serves affordable grilled chicken and fish dishes. Budget set lunch (€9–12). Alternatively, grab a bifana (pork sandwich) from a local snack bar for €3.
meals.dinner: Self-catering evening — buy fresh bread, local cheese, charcuterie, olives, and a bottle of Algarve wine from the supermarket. Enjoy on the terrace or in your room (€8–10 total for two).

day_by_day.notes: Silves is a must-visit for history lovers and is very budget-friendly. The castle is one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal. Check bus timetables at rede-expressos.pt or vamus.pt before going — services can be infrequent.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day at Praia de Armação de Pêra — a long, wide sandy beach about 15 minutes west of Lagoa by local bus (€2). Arrive early for a good spot. Swim, snorkel along the rock formations at the eastern end, and enjoy the calmer, sheltered waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the promenade of Armação de Pêra village. Visit the small whitewashed Chapel of Nossa Senhora da Rocha perched dramatically on a clifftop headland (free). Continue walking east along the cliffs toward the smaller Praia da Nossa Senhora da Rocha — a quieter, more secluded cove.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward Carvoeiro or Lagoa for the evening. Explore the local fish market area if still open in the late afternoon. Enjoy a sundowner at a clifftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Home-made or café stop in Lagoa — pão com manteiga (bread with butter, €1) and coffee (€0.80).
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Armação de Pêra beach — grilled sardines (sardinhas assadas, €7–9) — a quintessential Portuguese beach lunch. Wash down with a cold Sagres beer (€2).
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon Carvoeiro (look for the budget-friendly menu turístico) or O Escondidinho — a small local restaurant in Carvoeiro offering fresh grilled fish and Portuguese stews for €10–13 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Armação de Pêra has one of the longest beaches in the Algarve — great for long walks. The chapel viewpoint is particularly photogenic at golden hour. September sea temperatures are perfect for swimming.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Lagoa Saturday market (Mercado de Lagoa) — a lively local farmers' market with fresh produce, regional cheeses, smoked meats, honey, almond products, and Algarve wines. Stock up on picnic supplies and local specialties. This is a great opportunity to chat with local producers and sample for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a taxi to Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar, Lagoa (15 minutes). One of the Algarve's most awarded wineries offering guided vineyard tours and wine tastings. The basic tasting experience with 3–4 wines costs approximately €10–15 per person. Book ahead online. Enjoy the beautiful vineyard landscape and learn about Algarve DOC wines.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the accommodation. Sunset walk along the Praia da Marinha clifftops — the light at this time of year is spectacular. Prepare a relaxed evening with market purchases.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh pastries and local fruit from the Lagoa market (€3–4).
meals.lunch: Picnic at the winery or nearby — use market purchases: local bread, cheese, presunto, olives, and a bottle of purchased wine (€6–8).
meals.dinner: Tasca Bela in Lagoa — a no-frills local restaurant popular with residents. Daily specials board with dishes like bacalhau à brás (cod with eggs and potato) or grilled dourada (sea bream) for €9–12.

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales: quintadosvales.eu — book the tasting in advance, especially on weekends. The Algarve wine region is underrated and produces excellent reds from Negra Mole and Aragonez grapes. The Saturday market is one of the best in the region.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Portimão — take the local bus from Lagoa (€2.50, 25 minutes). Visit the Museu de Portimão (free on Sundays until 14:00 or €3 otherwise) — a fascinating museum inside a converted 19th-century sardine canning factory, telling the story of the Algarve's fishing and canning heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk across the bridge to Ferragudo — a charming, unspoiled fishing village across the Arade River (free pedestrian bridge). Explore the narrow cobblestone streets, the 16th-century Castelo de São João do Arade (exterior free), and the small fishing harbor. Have a relaxed afternoon exploring this hidden gem.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Portimão for the famous riverside sardine grills — the Portimão sardine festival area along the Arade riverfront is lined with casual restaurants and grill stalls. Enjoy the best grilled sardines in the Algarve at very low cost.

meals.breakfast: Café stop in Lagoa before the bus — coffee and pastel de nata (€1.80 total).
meals.lunch: O Barão in Ferragudo — a small, unpretentious local restaurant with excellent cataplana and grilled fish. Budget set lunch €9–11.
meals.dinner: Riverside sardine grill stalls in Portimão — a plate of 6 grilled sardines with bread, salad, and a beer for €8–10. This is the quintessential Algarve budget dinner experience.

day_by_day.notes: Ferragudo is one of the most authentic and least touristy villages in the Algarve — a real hidden gem. The contrast with nearby Portimão is striking. The Portimão Museum is genuinely excellent and free on Sundays — don't miss it.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the beaches around Carvoeiro in more depth. Walk the wooden boardwalk above Praia de Carvoeiro and descend to the beach. Continue east along the clifftop trail to Algar Seco — a dramatic natural rock formation with sea caves, arches, and pools carved into the limestone. Free to visit and explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle in Carvoeiro (€10–15/day from local rental shops) and cycle the inland roads through the orange and lemon groves, fig trees, and almond orchards of the Lagoa municipality. Visit the village of Estômbar and its pretty church. This is a relaxed, free way to see the authentic rural Algarve.
day_by_day.evening: Return bikes and freshen up. Walk or take a short taxi to dinner in Lagoa town center.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Lagoa — a local bakery with fresh bolas de Berlim (custard doughnuts, €1.20 each) and coffee (€0.80). A classic Algarve beach-town breakfast.
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Algar Seco — simple sandwiches, fresh orange juice squeezed on the spot (€2–4). Or bring your own from the mini-mercado.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Central de Lagoa — a classic old-school Portuguese restaurant in the town center. Bifanas, prego steaks, and grilled fish at very honest prices (€8–11 per person). House wine €1.50/glass.

day_by_day.notes: Algar Seco is free and absolutely stunning — one of the most photogenic spots in the Algarve. Go at low tide for the best rock pool exploration. Cycling inland is a great way to see the real Algarve beyond the beach strip.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lagos — take the bus from Lagoa (Rede Expressos or Eva, ~€4–5, 35–45 minutes). Start with the Mercado de Lagos (covered market) for fresh local produce. Then walk to Ponta da Piedade — the most spectacular sea cave and rock arch formation in the Algarve. The clifftop walk is free and breathtaking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Lagos old town: walk the ancient city walls, visit the Igreja de Santo António (beautiful azulejo tile interior, €4 with Museu Regional), and browse the cobblestone streets. Walk down to Meia Praia — a long, calm beach east of Lagos accessible on foot or by water taxi (€2). Swim and relax.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Lagos' vibrant but budget-friendly evening scene. The town has a lively mix of locals and travelers. Grab a drink at one of the small bars on Rua 25 de Abril before dinner.

meals.breakfast: At the Lagos market café — fresh orange juice (€1.50) and a pastel de nata (€1.20).
meals.lunch: Tasca do Gabão in Lagos — a tiny, beloved local tasca with a daily lunch special for €7–9 including bread, soup, main, and a drink. Arrive early as it fills up fast.
meals.dinner: O Camilo in Lagos (the casual version near the beach) or Manu's Lagos — grilled fish or chicken dishes for €10–13. Alternatively, grab a prego sandwich and eat on the beach (€4–5).

day_by_day.notes: Ponta da Piedade is best visited in the morning light. Boat tours from the Lagos marina to the caves cost €15–20 — optional but worthwhile. Lagos is one of the Algarve's most beautiful towns and very walkable. Return bus to Lagoa runs until late evening.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day — visit Adega do Cantor (Cliff Richard's famous winery) near Guia, Albufeira (20 minutes east of Lagoa). Tours and tastings available from €10–15 per person. The winery produces award-winning Vida Nova wines. Book ahead. Set in beautiful countryside with vineyard views.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the winery, continue to Albufeira old town (short taxi or bus). Walk the old Moorish town center, visit the clifftop viewpoint, and descend to Praia dos Pescadores (Fishermen's Beach) — a small, characterful beach flanked by colorful fishing boats. Explore the nearby sea cave (Gruta do Xorino) on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa/Carvoeiro. Relaxed evening at the accommodation with a bottle of wine purchased at the winery tasting.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — local bread, honey, and fresh fruit purchased from the market.
meals.lunch: Picnic in the vineyard or local snack bar near Guia — pão de queijo and local wine (€5–7). Guia is also famous for frango piri-piri (piri-piri chicken) — the Churrasqueira Ramires in Guia is legendary and very affordable (whole chicken ~€12, serves two).
meals.dinner: Churrasqueira Ramires in Guia (if not visited at lunch) — the birthplace of Algarve piri-piri chicken. A half chicken with chips and salad costs €7–9. One of the great budget dining experiences in Portugal.

day_by_day.notes: Adega do Cantor: adegadocantor.com — book in advance. Churrasqueira Ramires in Guia is a genuine institution (open since 1964) and is an essential Algarve food experience. Very budget-friendly and delicious.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at Praia da Marinha. Hire a kayak or paddleboard locally (€15–20/hour) and paddle along the coastline, exploring the sea caves and hidden grottoes only accessible by water. The cave system around Praia da Marinha is among the most beautiful in the Algarve.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus to Praia da Rocha in Portimão — one of the Algarve's most famous beaches, with dramatic red-orange cliffs and a long stretch of golden sand. Explore the ruins of the Fortaleza de Santa Catarina (fort, free exterior) overlooking the river mouth and beach.
day_by_day.evening: Portimão riverside for the evening. Walk along the Arade riverfront promenade and browse the outdoor terrace restaurants. Watch the fishing boats return to port.

meals.breakfast: Café near Praia da Marinha — coffee and fresh orange juice with a local pastry (€3–4).
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia da Rocha — grilled fish or a bifana sandwich (€5–8). Many beachside kiosks offer affordable lunch options in September.
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré in Portimão — a riverside tasca specializing in fresh fish and shellfish at honest local prices. Arroz de marisco (seafood rice) shared between two costs €18–22 total, making it affordable per person. House wine €1.50/glass.

day_by_day.notes: The kayaking around Praia da Marinha is a highlight of any Algarve trip — the limestone cave formations are extraordinary. September water clarity is excellent for snorkeling too. Praia da Rocha can be crowded even in September but is worth seeing.

day_by_day.morning: Inland adventure — take a bus or arrange a shared taxi to Monchique, in the Algarve's mountainous interior (approx. 45 minutes from Portimão, bus €4–5). Hike to the summit of Fóia — the highest peak in the Algarve at 902m — for panoramic views stretching from the Atlantic coast to the Spanish border on a clear day. The hike from Monchique town takes 2–3 hours return.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Monchique town — a charming mountain village with a ruined convent (Convento de Nossa Senhora do Desterro, free), artisan shops selling local medronho (arbutus berry brandy), and cork products. Sample medronho at a local shop (often free tasting, €5–8 per small bottle to buy).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa by bus or shared taxi. Relaxed evening — self-catered dinner or local restaurant in Carvoeiro.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at accommodation before departure — bread, coffee, local honey.
meals.lunch: Restaurante Central in Monchique — a hearty mountain lunch of carne de porco à alentejana (pork with clams) or grilled black pork (porco preto) for €10–13. Monchique is famous for its smoked sausages and mountain pork.
meals.dinner: Self-catered or a simple meal at a local Carvoeiro snack bar — pizza slice or tosta mista with a beer (€5–7).

day_by_day.notes: Monchique is a completely different side of the Algarve — lush, green, and cool compared to the coast. The medronho brandy is a local specialty — try before you buy. The Fóia summit road is also accessible by car/taxi if hiking isn't preferred. Wear layers as it can be cooler at altitude.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — return to your favorite beach from the trip, or explore Praia de Caneiros near Ferragudo (15 minutes from Lagoa) — a beautiful, sheltered cove with calm turquoise water, less visited than the main beaches. Perfect for a relaxed final swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa — the local wine cooperative right in Lagoa town, one of the oldest wine cooperatives in the Algarve (founded 1944). They offer informal tastings of their Algarve DOC wines for free or a nominal charge (€2–5). Buy a few bottles to take home (from €4–8/bottle). A great budget wine shopping experience.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — splurge slightly on your last evening in the Algarve. Walk to Carvoeiro for a special dinner with ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Café in Carvoeiro — full Portuguese breakfast: coffee, fresh orange juice, tosta mista, and pastel de nata (€5–6).
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Praia de Caneiros — fresh grilled fish or sardines with local bread (€7–9). Eat with your feet in the sand.
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Barril or A Varanda in Carvoeiro — a slightly elevated budget dinner to celebrate the end of the trip. Grilled sea bass (robalo) or monkfish cataplana for €14–18 per person. Share a bottle of Algarve white wine (€12–15). Enjoy the last Algarve sunset.

day_by_day.notes: The Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa is a gem for wine lovers on a budget — their wines are excellent value and you can taste before buying. Praia de Caneiros is one of the most underrated beaches in the Algarve. Pack your bags this evening for the morning departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — check out of Lagoa Boutique Stay. Take one last walk to the Praia da Marinha clifftop viewpoint for a final look at the stunning coastline. Pick up a few last-minute souvenirs from a local shop: local honey, almond sweets (Dom Rodrigo), dried figs, or a bottle of medronho or Algarve wine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Faro Airport (allow 1–1.5 hours). Take the Rede Expressos bus from Lagoa to Faro (€5–7, approximately 1 hour) or arrange a shared shuttle. Check in for your return flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Grab a final pastel de nata and espresso at the airport café (€2) before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Final Portuguese breakfast at a café near the accommodation — galão and a warm croissant or pastel de nata (€3–4). Savor it!
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Faro Airport café or bring snacks purchased at the local supermarket (€4–6).
meals.dinner: On the flight or at destination.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Faro. The Rede Expressos bus from Lagoa to Faro runs regularly — check timetables the night before at redex.pt. Total estimated budget for 13 days (excluding flights and accommodation): €400–550 per person, covering local transport, meals, activities, and wine tastings.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, pick up pre-booked rental car (recommended for Algarve exploration), and drive approximately 40 minutes west to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in, freshen up, and take a gentle first walk down to Praia da Marinha — consistently ranked one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. Explore the dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea arches, and crystal-clear turquoise coves. A short cliff-top trail offers stunning panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the area with a relaxed dinner nearby. Head to the village of Carvoeiro (10 min drive) for a stroll along the boardwalk and dinner at a local seafood restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Light bite at the airport or a café near Faro on the drive — try a pastel de nata and a bica (espresso).
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro — mid-range seafood spot with fresh grilled fish, cataplana (seafood stew), and local Algarve white wine. Budget ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: September is ideal in Algarve — warm (26–28°C), sea still perfect for swimming, crowds thinning after August. Rent a car at Faro Airport for maximum flexibility throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning at Praia da Marinha. Arrive early (before 10:00) to secure a spot on the small beach. Swim in the clear water, snorkel around the rock formations, and explore the sea caves accessible by swimming or kayak. Bring water shoes as the entry is rocky.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 15 minutes west to Algar Seco rock formations near Carvoeiro — a stunning coastal rock sculpture park with walkways, natural pools, and a cliffside bar. Spend an hour exploring, then relax at Praia do Carvoeiro for the afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Wine tasting evening: visit a local wine shop or wine bar in Lagoa town (10 min drive) — Lagoa is the heart of Algarve wine country. Ask for a tasting of regional Algarve DOC wines, particularly whites from Arinto and Síria grapes.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique stay or a local pastelaria — coffee, toast with butter and local honey, fresh orange juice.
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Algar Seco or pack a picnic from a local supermarket (Pingo Doce in Lagoa) — cheese, local bread, olives, and fruit.
meals.dinner: Tasca do Zé in Lagoa town — authentic Portuguese tasca with petiscos (small plates), grilled sardines, and regional wines. Budget ~€20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Marinha has very limited parking — arrive before 9:30 AM in September. The beach is accessible via a steep path with steps; not suitable for those with mobility issues.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 25 minutes west to Portimão and take a boat tour departing from the marina to explore the sea caves and grottos of Ponta da Piedade and the coastline between Lagos and Portimão. Tours typically last 1.5–2 hours and cost €20–30 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Lagos (15 min from Portimão) — one of Algarve's most charming historic towns. Explore the old town walls, the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos), Igreja de Santo António, and the lively Rua 25 de Abril. Browse local shops and galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Lagos for dinner — the town has a vibrant restaurant scene with excellent mid-range options along the marina and old town.

meals.breakfast: Café Correia or similar bakery in Portimão before the boat tour — galão (milky coffee) and a croissant or queijada (cheese tart).
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch in Lagos at Restaurante Adega da Marina — grilled dourada (sea bream) with potatoes and salad, house white wine. Budget ~€18–25 per person.
meals.dinner: No Pátio restaurant in Lagos old town — cozy courtyard setting, excellent cataplana and regional Alentejo/Algarve wines. Budget ~€28–38 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat cave tour in advance online or at the Portimão marina kiosk the evening before. Morning tours have calmer seas and better light for photography.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 20 minutes south of Lagos to Ponta da Piedade — the most spectacular coastal viewpoint in the Algarve. Walk the cliff-top trail (about 2 km round trip) at sunrise or early morning for golden light on the ochre rock formations and sea stacks. Optionally kayak through the sea arches (rentals available at the base).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia — a long, wide sandy beach east of Lagos (10 min drive) — perfect for a relaxed afternoon swim, sunbathing, and beach sports. The beach stretches 4 km and is far less crowded than smaller cove beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Carvoeiro/Lagoa area. Visit Quinta dos Vales winery (book in advance) near Estômbar for a late afternoon/early evening wine tasting tour of their vineyards and cellar, sampling their award-winning Algarve reds and whites.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the boutique stay before driving to Ponta da Piedade.
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Meia Praia — prego (steak roll), fresh fruit, and a cold beer or Sumol.
meals.dinner: O Leão de Porches in Porches village (10 min from Lagoa) — traditional Algarvian cuisine in a rustic setting, known for excellent arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice). Budget ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales wine tours must be booked in advance (quintadosvales.eu). Tours typically run at 10:00 and 15:00; opt for the 15:00 tour to fit the day's schedule. Cost ~€20–35 per person including tasting.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 45 minutes east to Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Visit the magnificent red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves), one of the best-preserved Moorish fortifications in Portugal. Explore the ramparts for panoramic views over the orange groves and hills.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves town: the Gothic Cathedral (Sé de Silves), the Archaeological Museum, and the charming riverside area along the Arade River. Browse the Saturday market if still running. Drive back via the Monchique foothills scenic route.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening back at base. Take a sunset walk along the cliff tops near Praia da Marinha and enjoy the golden hour light on the rock formations.

meals.breakfast: Café Central in Silves near the main square — fresh pastries, coffee, and fresh orange juice (Silves is famous for its oranges).
meals.lunch: Café Inglês in Silves — a beloved local institution built into the castle walls, serving light lunches and regional dishes. Budget ~€15–22 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the boutique stay's recommended local restaurant or O Cantinho do Zé in Lagoa — hearty Portuguese home cooking, bifanas, and local wine. Budget ~€18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Silves Castle entry ~€3.30 per person. Saturday mornings in Silves sometimes feature a local produce market near the riverside — great for picking up local almonds, figs, and honey.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 1 hour west to Sagres — the southwestern tip of continental Europe. Visit Cabo de São Vicente lighthouse, a dramatic headland where the Atlantic crashes against 60-metre cliffs. Walk the windswept clifftops and visit the small lighthouse museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Sagres Fortress (Fortaleza de Sagres) — a historic promontory fort associated with Henry the Navigator and the Age of Discovery. Walk the perimeter walls and explore the wind compass (Rosa dos Ventos). Nearby Praia do Beliche is a sheltered beach for a late afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Sagres before the drive back — the village has excellent fresh fish restaurants due to its active fishing port.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast from the boutique stay or stop at a pastelaria in Portimão on the way.
meals.lunch: A Sagres — simple seafood restaurant in Sagres village, excellent grilled tuna (atum) and percebes (barnacles). Budget ~€20–28 per person.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bossa Nova in Sagres — popular with locals and visitors, great grilled fish and seafood rice. Budget ~€22–30 per person. Drive back to Lagoa (1 hour).

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is noticeably windier and cooler than the rest of the Algarve — bring a light jacket. Cabo de São Vicente is free to visit; the lighthouse museum has a small entry fee. Sagres Fortress entry ~€3 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day. Slow morning at the boutique stay — enjoy breakfast at leisure, read by the pool (if available), or take a gentle yoga session or walk along the coastal path near Praia da Marinha.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 15 minutes to Armação de Pêra — a lively beach town with one of the longest beaches in the Algarve (Praia de Armação de Pêra). Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing on the wide sandy beach. Walk to the small white chapel (Nossa Senhora da Rocha) perched on the cliffs at the eastern end.
day_by_day.evening: Wine and cheese evening: visit a wine shop in Lagoa and pick up a bottle of Adega do Cantor (Cliff Richard's famous Algarve winery) or another regional label, pair with local cheeses, presunto, and olives for a relaxed in-room or terrace evening.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the boutique stay.
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar at Armação de Pêra — grilled chicken piri-piri, salad, and a cold drink.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Santola in Armação de Pêra — excellent seafood, particularly the arroz de marisco (seafood rice). Mid-range, budget ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally relaxed — a balanced trip needs rest days. Use the afternoon to reapply sunscreen, hydrate well, and avoid midday sun (12:00–15:00) which is still strong in September.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 1 hour east to Faro — the Algarve's capital city. Visit the Faro Old Town (Cidade Velha) inside the medieval walls: the Cathedral (Sé de Faro) with its rooftop views, the Bishop's Palace, and the Arco da Vila. Explore the charming cobblestone streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Igreja do Carmo and its haunting Bone Chapel (Capela dos Ossos) — a must-see baroque church. Then take a short ferry (15 min) to Ilha de Faro — a barrier island beach within the Ria Formosa Natural Park, with calm lagoon-side and open ocean-side beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Faro's vibrant restaurant scene before driving back to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Stop at Pastelaria Gardy in Faro — a classic 1960s café, famous for its Dom Rodrigos (local almond and egg yolk sweets) and coffee.
meals.lunch: Picnic on Ilha de Faro beach — pick up supplies from the Mercado Municipal in Faro (fresh bread, local cheese, fruit, cured meats).
meals.dinner: Restaurante Faz Gostos in Faro old town — elegant regional Portuguese cuisine in a historic house, excellent duck rice and regional wines. Budget ~€30–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Faro Cathedral rooftop offers stunning views over the lagoon and Ria Formosa — entry ~€3.50. Ferry to Ilha de Faro runs regularly from the pier near the old town (~€2.50 return). The Bone Chapel has a small entry fee.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 1 hour east to Tavira — widely considered the most beautiful town in the Algarve. Cross the Roman bridge over the Gilão River and explore the historic centre: the ruins of the Moorish castle, the Igreja da Misericórdia, and the distinctive four-sided rooftops (tesouro roofs) unique to Tavira.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the ferry (or water taxi) from Quatro Águas to Ilha de Tavira — a stunning barrier island with pristine natural beaches stretching for miles within the Ria Formosa park. Spend the afternoon swimming in the calm, clear water.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Tavira before driving back — Tavira has a sophisticated dining scene with excellent seafood.

meals.breakfast: Café Veneza in Tavira near the main square — traditional Portuguese breakfast.
meals.lunch: Beach restaurant on Ilha de Tavira — fresh grilled fish, salad, and local wine with your feet in the sand.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Quatro Águas near the ferry dock — famous for its clam dishes (ameijoas à Bulhão Pato) and fresh fish. Budget ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Ferry to Ilha de Tavira from Quatro Águas runs every 30 minutes in September (~€1.60 return). The island has several km of beach — walk further from the ferry for more secluded spots. Tavira is 1.5 hours from Lagoa — consider an early start.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated wine day: Drive to the Lagoa wine region for a morning visit to Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa — one of the oldest and most important wine cooperatives in the Algarve. Take a guided tour of the cellar and production facilities, followed by a tasting of their range of DOC Lagoa wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue wine exploration: drive 20 minutes to Adega do Cantor (Cliff Richard's winery) near Guia for a tasting of their acclaimed Vida Nova and Quinta do Miradouro labels. The estate has beautiful vineyard views and a welcoming tasting room.
day_by_day.evening: Wine-paired dinner: bring a bottle purchased during the day to a restaurant that allows BYO, or choose a restaurant with an extensive Algarve wine list to complement the day's learning.

meals.breakfast: Boutique stay breakfast — fuel up before the wine day.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local tasca in Lagoa town between tastings — avoid heavy meals to keep the palate fresh. Try bifanas and a glass of water.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Vila Lisa in Mexilhoeira Grande (near Portimão, 20 min drive) — legendary Algarve restaurant, exceptional regional cuisine, extensive wine cellar. A mid-range splurge. Budget ~€40–55 per person. Book well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Book Adega do Cantor tastings in advance at adegadocantor.com. Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa may require advance notice for tours — call ahead. Designate a driver or use a taxi/Uber for the wine day if both travelers wish to taste fully.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 45 minutes north into the Serra de Monchique — the green mountain range above the Algarve coast. Visit Caldas de Monchique, a charming spa village in a wooded valley, famous for its mineral springs. Walk the shaded valley paths and visit the historic spa buildings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue up to Monchique town — a traditional mountain village with craft shops, medronho (arbutus berry brandy) distilleries, and the ruins of a Franciscan convent. Drive to the summit of Fóia (902m) — the highest point in the Algarve — for sweeping views over the entire coast on clear days.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the coast. Enjoy a sunset aperitivo on the terrace at the boutique stay or at a clifftop bar near Carvoeiro.

meals.breakfast: Stop at a café in Caldas de Monchique — try local medronho brandy (just a small taste!) with coffee.
meals.lunch: Restaurante Central in Monchique town — hearty mountain cuisine: carne de porco preto (black pork), roasted chicken, and local vegetable soup. Budget ~€15–22 per person.
meals.dinner: A Ruína in Carvoeiro — popular local restaurant with grilled fish, shellfish, and regional wines on a terrace. Budget ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Serra de Monchique is noticeably cooler and greener than the coast — a refreshing contrast. Bring a light layer. The road to Fóia summit is narrow but paved and manageable. Look for local honey, jams, and medronho to bring home as gifts.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning — return to Praia da Marinha one last time for a long, leisurely swim and a final appreciation of the stunning cliffs and water. Alternatively, explore nearby Praia da Benagil (15 min drive) — famous for the Benagil Sea Cave (Algar de Benagil), one of the most photographed natural features in Portugal. Take a kayak or SUP tour into the cave (book in advance).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Saturday market in Lagoa or Portimão for local produce, crafts, and souvenirs. Pick up local almonds, figs, carob products, medronho, and regional wines to take home. Spend the late afternoon packing and relaxing.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — celebrate the trip with a special meal at one of the area's best restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Boutique stay breakfast — enjoy it fully before the beach morning.
meals.lunch: Beachside snack at Benagil or Marinha — keep it light before the farewell dinner.
meals.dinner: Bon Bon Restaurant in Carvoeiro — Michelin-starred, offering a tasting menu of creative Algarve cuisine. A special splurge for the final night. Book weeks in advance. Budget ~€80–120 per person for the tasting menu with wine pairing. Alternatively, A Forja in Lagos for excellent mid-range regional food at ~€30–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Benagil Cave kayak tours must be booked well in advance — try Kayak Adventures Algarve or similar operators. The cave is only accessible by water. Saturday markets in the Algarve are excellent for authentic local products and souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Slow farewell morning. Take a final walk along the coastal cliff path near the boutique stay to soak in the views one last time. Pack, check out, and say goodbye to the hosts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Faro Airport (approximately 40–45 minutes from Lagoa). Allow extra time to return the rental car, check in, and clear security. If the flight is in the afternoon or evening, stop in Faro town for a final coffee and pastel de nata at Pastelaria Gardy.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Carry home memories, a bottle of Algarve wine, local almonds, and the golden light of the Algarve coast.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the boutique stay — enjoy the terrace and morning light.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a quick stop at a café in Faro — prego no pão (steak sandwich) and a bica for the road.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 — confirm with the boutique stay. Faro Airport is small but can get busy on Sunday afternoons — arrive at least 2 hours before departure. Duty-free at Faro has a reasonable selection of Portuguese wines and spirits.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Walk & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Walk the clifftop trail connecting Marinha to Benagil and take a refreshing swim in the sheltered coves below.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Faro Airport to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay (approximately 45 minutes). Settle into your suite, unpack, and enjoy a welcome glass of chilled Vinho Verde on your private terrace overlooking the Atlantic.
day_by_day.afternoon: After freshening up, take a leisurely first stroll along the Praia da Marinha clifftop path to soak in the dramatic golden limestone scenery and turquoise waters. A gentle introduction to the Algarve's most iconic coastline — no strenuous hiking, just panoramic views and the warm September sea breeze.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a highly regarded local restaurant in Lagoa or Carvoeiro. Recommended: Vila Joya (Albufeira, short drive) or Restaurante Bon Bon (Carvoeiro) — both Michelin-starred establishments offering creative modern Portuguese cuisine with exceptional wine lists. Toast your arrival with a glass of premium Alentejo red.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (arrival day — enjoy welcome refreshments at the hotel upon check-in)
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread prepared by the boutique stay or a quick stop at a local pastelaria near the airport/en route for a Pastel de Nata and espresso
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon, Carvoeiro — Michelin-starred tasting menu with paired Portuguese wines (book in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in if possible given 13:00 arrival. Keep the afternoon relaxed to recover from travel. Confirm dinner reservation at Bon Bon well ahead of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Walk & Swim — embark on the signature experience of your stay. Explore the dramatic golden limestone cliffs, hidden sea caves, and crystal-clear rock pools of Praia da Marinha, consistently ranked among Europe's most beautiful beaches. Swim in the sheltered turquoise coves and snorkel around the limestone arches. Bring reef shoes for the rocky entry points.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat tour departing from Benagil or Carvoeiro — cruise along the stunning Algarve coastline, enter the famous Benagil Sea Cave (Algar de Benagil) from the water, explore hidden grottos, and anchor in secluded bays for swimming and snorkelling. Opt for a premium private charter with a skipper and onboard refreshments for a truly luxurious experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at the hotel terrace watching the golden hour light on the cliffs. Dinner at O Castelo Restaurant in Carvoeiro — a refined clifftop restaurant with panoramic ocean views, exceptional fresh seafood, and a strong regional wine selection.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay — fresh local fruit, artisan bread, smoked Alentejo charcuterie, local cheeses, and freshly squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Light picnic basket prepared by the hotel or fresh seafood lunch aboard the private boat charter
meals.dinner: O Castelo, Carvoeiro — fresh Atlantic lobster or grilled turbot with a bottle of premium Alvarinho white wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat charter at least 2–3 days in advance, especially in September. Bring high-SPF sunscreen, a hat, and water shoes for the coastal walk. September water temperature is ideal for swimming (~22–24°C).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia do Carvalho and Praia de Benagil — two of the Algarve's most enchanting hidden beaches, both within a short drive or scenic coastal walk from the hotel. Praia do Carvalho is accessible via a tunnel carved through the cliff, offering a wonderfully secluded atmosphere. Swim and relax on the golden sand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wine tasting experience at Adega do Cantor (Guia, Albufeira) — the celebrated winery co-founded by Sir Cliff Richard, producing award-winning Vida Nova and Onda Nova wines. Enjoy a guided tour of the vineyards and cellar, followed by a structured tasting of their premium red, white, and rosé selections paired with local charcuterie and cheese.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a private in-suite dining experience or a relaxed dinner at a local favourite. Recommended: Restaurante Borda d'Água in Porches — a charming, intimate restaurant on the lagoon serving outstanding traditional Algarvian cuisine with a modern touch.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Charcuterie, artisan cheese, and wine pairing at Adega do Cantor during the tasting experience
meals.dinner: Restaurante Borda d'Água, Porches — cataplana de marisco (seafood cataplana) with a bottle of Vida Nova Rosé

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Adega do Cantor wine tasting tour. The winery is approximately 20 minutes from the hotel. Consider purchasing a case of their premium wines to be shipped home.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Visit the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves, one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal, and the Gothic Cathedral (Sé de Silves). Wander through the charming cobbled streets of this historic town perched above the Arade River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wine tasting at Quinta dos Vales — one of the Algarve's most prestigious wine estates, located near Estômbar (15 minutes from Silves). Enjoy a premium guided tour of the estate's sculpture garden, vineyards, and wine cellar, followed by a tasting of their award-winning Algarve wines including their celebrated Marquês dos Vales Grande Reserva. The estate also features impressive outdoor art installations.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Silves at Restaurante Marisqueira Rui — an institution in Silves and widely regarded as one of the best seafood restaurants in the Algarve. Famous for their grilled fish, shellfish, and the freshest local catch. Pair with a crisp Algarve white wine.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Light tapas and wine at Quinta dos Vales estate during the tasting
meals.dinner: Marisqueira Rui, Silves — grilled sea bass or whole baked turbot with seasonal vegetables

day_by_day.notes: Silves is approximately 30 minutes from the hotel. Pre-book the Quinta dos Vales premium tasting experience. The castle can be warm in the afternoon, so morning exploration is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Praia de Albandeira and Praia do Paraíso beach morning — two of the most secluded and beautiful small beaches in the central Algarve, both within 10 minutes of the hotel. Albandeira is framed by towering cliffs and a natural arch, offering exceptional snorkelling. Arrive early to secure the best spots before day visitors arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking and stand-up paddleboarding along the Praia da Marinha coastline — rent premium equipment or book a guided sea kayaking tour to explore the sea caves, arches, and hidden grottoes that are inaccessible on foot. This stretch of coast is arguably the most spectacular in all of Portugal for sea kayaking.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset aperitivo on the hotel terrace, followed by dinner at Restaurante Vila Lisa in Mexilhoeira Grande — a legendary, intimate restaurant in a converted farmhouse offering exquisitely prepared traditional Algarvian and Alentejo dishes. One of the most authentic fine-dining experiences in the region.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Fresh local seafood at a beach kiosk at Praia de Albandeira or a packed gourmet picnic from the hotel
meals.dinner: Restaurante Vila Lisa, Mexilhoeira Grande — slow-roasted lamb with migas and a bottle of premium Alentejo red

day_by_day.notes: Book the sea kayaking tour in advance. Vila Lisa is approximately 35 minutes from the hotel — reservations are essential and should be made weeks in advance as it is a very small, sought-after restaurant.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lagos — one of the most beautiful and historic towns in the Algarve. Explore the old town, the 16th-century city walls, the Igreja de Santo António (a baroque masterpiece), and the fascinating Slave Market Museum. Stroll along the esplanade and browse the artisan boutiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the extraordinary Ponta da Piedade — a spectacular headland just south of Lagos featuring towering golden rock formations, sea stacks, arches, and emerald grottos. Take a private boat tour from Lagos marina to explore the caves and arches from the water. Alternatively, walk the clifftop paths for breathtaking panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Lagos at Restaurante Adega da Marina — a premium seafood and Portuguese cuisine restaurant in a beautifully converted wine cellar with an exceptional wine list. Or opt for the upscale Casinha do Petisco for creative modern Portuguese small plates.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante O Camelo or Restaurante Nah Nah Bah in Lagos — both offer excellent fresh local cuisine in a relaxed setting
meals.dinner: Adega da Marina, Lagos — Atlantic prawns piri-piri, grilled octopus, and a bottle of premium Vinho Verde

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is approximately 35 minutes from the hotel. Consider hiring a private driver for the day to allow full enjoyment of the wine tasting and evening dinner. Ponta da Piedade boat tours are popular — book ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at leisure — enjoy a slow breakfast on the hotel terrace, followed by a spa treatment or private yoga session if available at the boutique stay. Alternatively, take a peaceful morning swim at the uncrowded Praia da Marinha before the day visitors arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Porches Pottery (Olaria Algarve) — the most famous traditional hand-painted ceramic studio in the Algarve, located just 10 minutes from the hotel. Watch artisans at work, learn about the centuries-old craft, and select premium hand-painted pieces as luxury souvenirs. Followed by a visit to the nearby Lagoa Wine Cooperative (Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa) for a tasting of the region's distinctive Lagoa DOC wines.
day_by_day.evening: Private chef dinner experience at the boutique stay — arrange for a local private chef to prepare a bespoke multi-course dinner in your suite or on the private terrace, featuring the finest local ingredients: fresh seafood from the Portimão market, Algarvian figs, local almonds, and premium regional wines. A truly intimate and memorable experience.

meals.breakfast: Extended leisurely gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local café in Lagoa town — try a prego no pão (steak sandwich) or fresh grilled sardines
meals.dinner: Private chef multi-course dinner at the boutique stay — menu tailored to your preferences with paired wines

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the private chef experience at least 3–4 days in advance through the hotel concierge. This is an ideal mid-trip treat and rest day. The Porches Pottery workshop is free to visit; premium pieces can be shipped internationally.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Mercado de Portimão (Portimão Municipal Market) — explore the vibrant local food market brimming with fresh Atlantic fish, regional cheeses, cured meats, seasonal fruits, and artisan produce. A wonderful immersion into authentic Algarvian daily life. Pick up local delicacies for snacking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Boat trip on the Arade River — depart from Portimão marina on a private luxury river cruise up the scenic Arade River to Silves, passing through lush riverbanks, orange groves, and traditional fishing villages. Enjoy onboard refreshments and a guided commentary on the region's history and ecology.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Restaurante Titanic in Portimão — one of the Algarve's most celebrated traditional seafood restaurants, famous for their cataplana dishes and grilled fresh fish. A local institution beloved by both residents and discerning visitors.

meals.breakfast: Quick espresso and pastel de nata at the Portimão market before exploring
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the Arade River boat — fresh market produce, local cheeses, cured meats, and chilled Alvarinho
meals.dinner: Restaurante Titanic, Portimão — cataplana de amêijoas (clam cataplana) and grilled dourada with a bottle of premium Algarve white

day_by_day.notes: Portimão is approximately 20 minutes from the hotel. The Arade River private boat cruise should be booked in advance. The market is most vibrant in the morning — arrive by 9:00 for the best selection.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — drive to the dramatic southwestern tip of Europe. Visit the historic Fortaleza de Sagres, used by Henry the Navigator as his legendary school of navigation. Walk the clifftops at Cabo de São Vicente, Europe's most southwesterly point, where the Atlantic stretches endlessly to the horizon. A profoundly atmospheric and awe-inspiring experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the wild beaches of the Costa Vicentina near Sagres — Praia do Beliche (a dramatic sheltered cove below the cliffs) and Praia da Mareta (a beautiful crescent of sand in Sagres bay). Swim in the cooler, wilder Atlantic waters of this protected natural park coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Sagres at A Tasca, or drive back towards Lagos for dinner at Restaurante Adega da Marina. Alternatively, stop at the charming Restaurante O Telheiro do Infante near Sagres for outstanding fresh fish with dramatic ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay before the early departure
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish lunch at a local restaurant in Sagres village — try grilled sea bream or sardines
meals.dinner: O Telheiro do Infante, Sagres — grilled monkfish with garlic and coriander, paired with a crisp Alvarinho

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is approximately 1 hour from the hotel. Consider hiring a private driver. Cabo de São Vicente can be windy even in September — bring a light jacket. The scenery is extraordinary at golden hour if you time the return journey accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Premium golf morning at Penina Hotel & Golf Resort or Amendoeira Golf Resort — both world-class courses within 30–40 minutes of the hotel. Penina, designed by Sir Henry Cotton, is one of Portugal's most prestigious golf courses. Book a tee time and enjoy 18 holes in the beautiful Algarve landscape. (If golf is not of interest, substitute with a morning spa session or a return visit to Praia da Marinha.)
day_by_day.afternoon: Wine and olive oil tasting experience at Quinta da Tôr — a beautiful estate near Loulé producing excellent Algarve wines and premium extra-virgin olive oil. Enjoy a guided tour of the olive groves and vineyards, followed by a paired tasting of their estate wines and oils with local bread and charcuterie.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo — a superb seafood restaurant on the banks of the Arade River estuary with exceptional views of Portimão and the river mouth. Famous for their perfectly grilled fresh fish and shellfish. One of the most scenic dining settings in the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the golf club restaurant or at Quinta da Tôr during the tasting
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste, Ferragudo — grilled whole sea bass with roasted vegetables and a bottle of premium Algarve white wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the golf tee time well in advance. Quinta da Tôr tasting should also be pre-arranged. Ferragudo is a beautifully preserved fishing village worth exploring before dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Loulé — the cultural and artisan capital of the Algarve. Explore the spectacular Moorish-influenced covered market (Mercado de Loulé), the medieval castle, and the charming old town with its whitewashed chimneys and artisan workshops producing copper, leather, and ceramics. Browse the luxury boutiques and artisan galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium wine tasting at Herdade dos Pimenteiros near Loulé — a boutique estate producing some of the most refined Algarve wines, with a beautiful setting among rolling hills and vineyards. Enjoy an in-depth guided tasting of their reserve wines paired with local cheeses and charcuterie. Alternatively, visit Quinta do Francês for a similarly excellent boutique wine experience.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Restaurante Henrique Leis in Almancil — a legendary Michelin-starred restaurant offering innovative Franco-Portuguese cuisine in an elegant setting. Chef Henrique Leis has been one of the Algarve's culinary stars for decades. An unmissable fine-dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Fresh local produce from Loulé market — artisan bread, regional cheeses, smoked sausages, and fresh fruit enjoyed as a picnic
meals.dinner: Restaurante Henrique Leis, Almancil — chef's tasting menu with full wine pairing (book months in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Loulé is approximately 30 minutes from the hotel. Almancil is approximately 25 minutes. Reservations at Henrique Leis are essential and should be made well before the trip. This is one of the finest dining experiences in Portugal.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning at Praia da Marinha — savour this extraordinary beach one last time. Swim in the crystal-clear waters, explore the rock pools at low tide, and take a final clifftop walk to photograph the stunning limestone scenery. Pack a gourmet picnic from the hotel for a leisurely beach morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury spa afternoon at the boutique stay or at a nearby premium spa — enjoy a traditional Portuguese massage, a scrub with local sea salt and almond oil, and a relaxing facial. Alternatively, visit the thermal spa at Monchique in the hills above the Algarve for a unique natural spa experience (approximately 45 minutes from the hotel).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at the hotel or at one of the Algarve's finest restaurants — Vila Joya in Albufeira (two Michelin stars, one of Portugal's greatest restaurants) for the ultimate celebratory finale. Chef Dieter Koschina's cuisine is extraordinary, and the wine cellar is among the finest in the country.

meals.breakfast: Extended gourmet farewell breakfast at the boutique stay — order everything from the menu
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the beach at Praia da Marinha — champagne, local cheeses, fresh fruit, and artisan bread
meals.dinner: Vila Joya, Albufeira — two-Michelin-star tasting menu with full wine pairing. One of the most exceptional dining experiences in Portugal (book months in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Vila Joya reservations must be made months in advance and require a credit card guarantee. This is the perfect farewell dinner to close a luxury Algarve trip. Begin packing this evening for the next day's departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — enjoy a last slow breakfast on the hotel terrace with views of the Atlantic. Take a final short walk to the clifftop at Praia da Marinha to say farewell to the golden cliffs and turquoise sea. Check out of the boutique stay and arrange private luxury transfer to Faro Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to Faro Airport (approximately 45 minutes). Allow ample time for check-in and security. Browse the airport shops for last-minute Portuguese gifts — Pastéis de Nata from a local bakery, a bottle of Vida Nova wine, or artisan Algarve almonds and figs.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Carry wonderful memories of 13 extraordinary days exploring the beaches, wines, cuisine, and culture of the Algarve.

meals.lunch: Light lunch at Faro Airport or a quick stop at a café in Faro old town if time allows before the flight
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the airport transfer the evening before. Consider purchasing a selection of premium Algarve wines (Vida Nova, Quinta dos Vales Grande Reserva, Quinta do Francês) to take home as souvenirs. Confirm baggage allowance for wine bottles. Tip the hotel staff generously for an outstanding stay.
